newsitem.title: UK: UK details companies to pay utility tax.
newsitem.headline: UK details companies to pay utility tax.

text.p: Britain on Wednesday detailed the companies which are subject to the windfall tax on privatised utilities which Chancellor of the Exchequer (Finance Minister) Gordon Brown announced in his budget.

The Inland Revenue said in a statement the tax would be charged at a rate of 23 percent on the difference between company value at the time of flotation and company value calculated by reference to profits over a period of up to four years following privatisation. The expected yield is around 5.2 billion stg, the Revenue said.
The following are the companies affected. The government and the Revenue gave no breakdown of amounts expected to be paid by individual companies.
Airport operator BAA Plc
British Energy Plc
Former British Gas companies BG Plc and Centrica Plc
British Telecommunications Plc
National Power Plc
Northern Ireland Electricity Plc
PowerGen Plc
Scottish Hydro-Electric Plc
Scottish Power Plc, which also owns which owns Southern Water and Manweb
Railtrack Plc
The regional electricity companies (RECs) and water and sewage companies --
London Electricity, owned by Entergy Corp of the U.S.
Northern Electric, owned by CE Electric of the U.S.
East Midlands Electricity, owned by Dominion Resources Inc of the U.S.
South Western Electricity, owned by Southern Co of the U.S.
Seeboard, owned by Central & South West Corp of the U.S.
Midlands Electricity, owned by Avon Energy, a joint venture between GPU Inc and CINergy of the U.S.
Hyder Plc, which owns Welsh Water and South Wales Electricity
United Utilities Plc, which owns North West Water and Norweb
Southern Electric Plc
Eastern Electric, now part of the Energy Group Plc
Yorkshire Electricity, now owned by American Electric Power and Public Service Co of Colorado
Northumbrian Water, owned by Lyonnaise des Eaux SA of France
Anglian Water Plc
Thames Water Plc
Wessex Water Plc
Severn Trent Plc
South West Water Plc
Yorkshire Water Plc
